title: Small Depression band with Bob Anthony
summary: During the Depression he formed a small band that worked Delacroix Island dances.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Bob Antony. Bob Antony. Anthony. I don't know him. Yeah, I think he was, he spent a while in the United States Navy with us, but he was, went into TB sickness, was in the hospital for quite a while, right after he got out of the Navy. And he, we made, we used to play down.

Someone say he's living, some say he's dead. In fact, I don't know, I don't know where he's in contact. Yeah, I haven't been. Wouldn't know where to contact Bob. I haven't seen Bob in about five years. But we worked all down in Buris, and then we called a place to call it down, this place down in Seminole Parish, they call it, not Buris, Delico Island. Oh yeah. We used to work down there every Saturday night, different dances, plus local around the city, different engagements like that. Then formerly I went and worked out, and Depression come on, and I went and worked out on the WPA. First it was ERA, then the WPA. And there was forming bands at a place that called Patonis, used to be a keeper at the old parish prison, Tulane and Broad. And he had a restaurant in a dance place on Domain between Decatur and Charless, Patonis. And he had a little four piece band up there then playing nightly, which consisted of Ellie Big Ar drums and Walter Dacu playing the piano. And I think he had Charlie loved playing trumpet, if I'm not mistaken. It was a three or four piece band. And they left us used it, and they formed the ERA band. And they sent a letter on the field for me to come and join that outfit, which was sent by Louis Dumain, formed the old trumpet player, Louis Dumain.
